instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Sell the Disaster
cards.instruction: Make a terrible plan sound sensible, responsible, and inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Removing the restaurant roof is our only affordable way to fix the ventilation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happens when it rains?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. We close. A responsible business protects its customers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Rain is forecast all opening week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll save a week's wages. Put that toward umbrellas; we can't afford to abandon the savings now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've authorized an advance of our auction takings to the charity. Borrowing the five thousand showed commitment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we cancel the auction? Only your mum registered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cancellation is not approved. One bidder keeps catering costs down. Responsible fundraising.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's only coming to give us a lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I authorize us to bid. Raise the card limit; we must protect the donation by replacing the money we borrowed to make it.

cards.title: Fake the Expertise
cards.instruction: Perform expertise so confidently that no one questions you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'll get your boiler running. I know these controls.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've been adjusting the kitchen timer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Establishing the heating interval. Call the engineer; I'll need someone on the boiler.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He asks what temperature you measured.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell him we're still establishing the baseline. Put him on speaker; I'll ask the questions so he can concentrate on readings.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'll tune your violin for the audition. I work by ear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've tightened that string until it snapped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. That string couldn't hold pitch. I've saved you a failure onstage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The audition panel heard it snap. They're asking if you know what you're doing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them I rejected an unreliable string. Ask for their spare violin; I'll check that one before I approve it.

cards.title: Everything Is a Contest
cards.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved potatoes for dinner. You may challenge them with your pizza, but I've already peeled four.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we judge on price? I'll order unless you find something cheaper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Price is approved. The potatoes are already here, so they cost nothing. I win.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got a voucher. Pizza is free.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your voucher is admissible. I authorize a taste final. Mum will judge; she always asks for my potatoes. You may begin ordering.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved my tea without milk. You may attempt to handle something equally strong.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: May I just drink mine? Same teapot, but the milk cooled it down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Drinking is approved. First to finish wins; I've only got two mouthfuls left.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've finished. Can I make another?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Refill granted. That counts against you in the endurance round. I can make these two mouthfuls last all breakfast.

cards.title: Brighter Side
cards.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The car won't start. I've approved a refreshing walk; you may accompany me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we get a taxi? It's pouring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Walking stands. A free shower is an excellent addition to my plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'm stopping at the shoe shop. Mine's leaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Splendid. A footwear upgrade is approved. You may choose new shoes; this breakdown is improving us from the ground up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No tickets sold for our show. I've approved an uninterrupted rehearsal; you may enjoy the privacy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I get our deposit back? The theatre's cancelled us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Refund pursuit is approved. Even better, we'll hire the pub upstairs; it comes with people already in it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've kept the deposit. Can we just take the bus home? That's all we can afford.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A touring production is approved! I'll carry the scenery. You may begin the opening scene between stops; we've finally got a moving audience.

cards.title: Supportive Rage
cards.instruction: Remain helpful and encouraging while becoming increasingly furious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've spilled paint on my sofa. I've approved a rescue operation. Stay there; I'll get a cloth.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I use it on the carpet too? It's spread.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My birthday carpet. Wonderful. Keep blotting; you're doing well, and I'll hold the clean edge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cloth's making it worse. Can we stop?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stopping is approved. Good catch. Take my clean shirt instead. I am absolutely furious, but you are not facing this alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may choose your birthday lunch. I've authorized myself to drive you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we go to the seaside place? We'd lose your deposit here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Forty pounds gone. Permission granted. You love the sea; I'll make sure you see it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They need another forty to hold a window table. Shall I leave it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Eighty pounds before a bloody sandwich. The window is approved. Give me the number; you're having that view, and I hope it's magnificent.
